Mr. Savo Bojanovic sat on trials of Serbs who had committed offences against non-Serbs. On one occasion, he conducted an investigation of two Serbian perpetrators who had allegedly raped two Muslim women. Interviews were conducted with the victims who were very grateful that the investigation was being carried out and that a trial would begin. The investigations were continued and the suspects were remanded into custody. However, it was established that the perpetrators were not members of the army and the case was handed over to the civilian judicial authorities. Mr. Savo Bojanovic is aware that the relationship between the Bijeljina Military Court and the regular courts was correct and was based on the valid regulations. The relationship of the Military Court and the competent command of the East Bosnia Corps was mutually respectful and was based on legality and respect of procedure. Savo Bojanovic was never ordered by anyone as to how to judge his cases, and he was not aware that any of these -- his colleagues had been given any suggestions either. In February 1993, Savo Bojanovic was on call when the military police called because there was a double homicide in the yard of Vanekov Mlin prison. An investigation team including Savo Bojanovic went out the same evening and conducted an on-site investigation. It was established that during the afternoon, a unit of the 2nd Krajina Brigade stopped to refuel at this barracks very close to the prison. The soldiers asked the prison guards if they could phone their relatives. During this, a soldier noticed a prisoner who had previously murdered the soldier's relatives. When the man's name was shouted, he began to run. He was caught and his head cut off. Another prisoner was also killed. The Military Court reported all this to the International Committee of the Red Cross. Mr. Savo Bojanovic is not aware of the murder of 40 to 80 civilians by the MUP of RS. He considers this to be a fabricated story. Savo Bojanovic declares with full responsibility that the work of the Bijeljina Military Court was not discriminatory at all in terms of religion or ethnic background or of either the defendants or victims. He also declares that the Military Court and judges were not pressured by military or civilian authorities. The work of the court was based solely on the application of and respect for the regulations and laws valid at that time. Having had contact members of the military police and VRS security organs, Savo Bojanovic stated that they were professionally trained for their work, which assisted in finding the perpetrators of criminal offences. [Interpretation] 1D7240. Could we please see that document now and we'd like to ask the witness to provide an explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It has to do with paragraph 11 of your statement.

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what this document is.

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: As I've already stated in my written statement that is attached here, on that day, in the late evening hours, the military police --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, Judge. Do you see the document on the screen? That's the document that I'm asking you about.

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please explain to us what this document represents.

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: This is a ruling on releasing Jurosevic and Cvetkovic from custody.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you explain the essence of this document. You signed this as investigating judge, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you explain to us now why they were released from custody, what the detention policy was, and how it was regulated.

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: We applied the Law on Criminal Procedure of the SFRY clearly stating the reasons for remanding persons into custody. As you can see here, on the 22nd of January, 1993, by applying that law, we passed this decision. They had been in custody for two months and even more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, what is the procedure after that when a person is released from custody?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: That does not mean relief from criminal responsibility. It just means that the suspect has been released from custody, that the legally prescribed requirements have been met for releasing such a person from custody. However, criminal proceedings continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you assist us how this is relevant, Mr. Robinson?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: I think Dr. Karadzic is best placed to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Excellencies, the Prosecution often suggests that someone was released from custody, and then we have brought here a completely independent very prominent judge who explains his own decision on releasing a person from custody when there was no reasons to keep these persons into custody any longer. It states that this does not have anything to do with his own free will but, rather, there have to be formal reasons for doing that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Any objection, Ms. Sutherland?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We'll receive it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D3078, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. 1D25456. Could we please see that document now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It has to do with paragraph 14 of your statement. However, please look at the document that is on the screen. Can you tell us what this judgement shows? Who is the perpetrator, who is the victim, especially in relation to ethnic background?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Rade Mihajlovic is the convicted person here, and he was convicted on the basis of Article 36 of the relevant law. Very well. I shall speak slower. And the crime was committed against Tabakovic Enes. I cannot see it very well. I think the first name is Enes, an ethnic Muslim. The killing was committed in the barracks in Bijeljina in 1992. This is a decision, a judgement of the regular District Court in Bijeljina. However, the investigation in this case was conducted by the Military Court in Bijeljina. When the military prosecutor's office brought charges against Rade Mihajlovic, I was in charge of this indictment, and I carried out certain procedural matters. However, the person was a fugitive. He [Realtime transcript read in error "I"] had been in custody but had been unlawfully [as interpreted] released. So then I asked for an APB to be issued against this person. I did not become aware of the outcome of this case. I see that in 2001, it was the regular District Court in Bijeljina that passed this judgement, because after the war the Military Courts were disbanded.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Again, I ask you kindly to speak a bit slower. Could you please tell us what the sentence was in the case of this accused person and what the maximum sentence was at the time for such a crime?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: He was convicted -- he was sentenced to ten years, and the maximum sentence at the time for that kind of crime was 20 years.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. I probably need your assistance. Line 4. It should read: "He had been in custody," not the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The accused person was in custody.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: At the time what was the maximum sentence for murder?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Twenty years.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In 2001 or in 1992?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Believe me, I left the judiciary, but I think that the maximum sentence hasn't changed. I think that the maximum sentence was 20 years in prison at that point in time as well.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this document be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So you are tendering only this page, first page?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I think it's not a very long judgement. It's three or four pages, I think. Well, not necessarily the entire case file, but it's sufficient to see that Judge Bojanovic was involved in the investigation and also to see the judgement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You relied on --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] An objection, please, Your Honours. I was not in charge of the investigation. I was in charge of issuing the indictment because I was president of the chamber at that point in time. Since the accused person was a fugitive and he probably returned after the war when the military courts were abolished, so then the case was deferred to a regular court, and then it was the District Court that passed the judgement in 2001 with regard to this particular case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What does that mean in terms of such fugitives? What happens to the case?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, when the person is a fugitive, then an APB is issued. The person becomes a wanted person. I don't know whether he was extradited or not. I know that this person was in Switzerland. I don't know whether he himself surrendered, but this is a detail I'm not familiar with.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The judgement is the first five pages. This is a case that was started by Judge Bojanovic, and as soon as the accused person was present again, the proceedings were brought to an end.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think that's sufficient for this witness's evidence, and given -- and given that the B/C/S is a document of 33 pages, I think it's fair enough to admit only the first page, which was shown to the witness. Yes, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, in fact that's D01479.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Oh, really. We admitted this. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bojanovic, you were so kind as to bring us personally a few court decisions.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D07830. Could we please have a look at that now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Unfortunately, they haven't been translated yet, so I'm going to ask you to give us an exhaustive explanation as to what all of this is about.

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I still have the document on the monitor.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D07830.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We have an order on detention for two people -- three people.

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Four.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what it's about?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It concerns the proceedings against four accused who, in March 1993, committed the crime of robbery by having gained entry to a family home.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If there's sensitive information contained, either skip that or ask to go into private session. I leave it up to you as a judge.

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Am I allowed to refer to the names of the victims?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Depending on the nature of crime.

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it concerns rape.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Explain to us who the perpetrators were, especially in terms of their ethnicity, who the victims were, and what was the conclusion of the proceedings?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it concerns four members of the VRS, four young men from a village near Bijeljina. On the date referred to, having broken into the house, stole some property, gold and money, and then the first accused raped a person, Petar Trifunovic. The second accused was involved in the basic form of sexual assault. On this occasion, the investigating judge decided to issue the decision on detention, and they were caught the same day. Since they were members of the VRS and they were in uniform, the case was transferred to the Military Court in Bijeljina. I continued being in charge of investigations in this case, and the accused were in custody. They were held for 30 days as decided by the Basic Court in Bijeljina. Following the dead-line of one month since the investigation was still ongoing, I proposed -- and I handed over that document to the Defence, I proposed to the chamber of the court to act in accordance with the Law on Criminal Procedure to extend their custody for another 60 days. Which is what was done by virtue of this decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us how the proceedings concluded?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the case was closed by the handing down of a judgement. The first accused was proclaimed guilty for robbery and rape and received a sentence for three years. The second accused was charged with robbery, indecent acts, and received a sentence of two and a half years. The third accused, Milenko Stojanovic, was pronounced guilty for the crime of robbery and received a year and a half years. And the fourth accused received a sentence of one year and three months. Although I may be wrong on the exact length of sentences, but it's around that period.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have 1D07831. It can form part of the same exhibit if we wish.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: As for the range of sentences, did they fall within the legal regulations as prescribed by law?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Based on the jurisprudence we applied in such cases, given the fact that the Military Court was in charge of the most serious crimes such as murder, rape, and theft, we followed a uniformed sentencing policy which was decided on during joint meetings of the judges of the court in contact with the Supreme Military Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we go down to the bottom of the page. It is your document of the 24th of April, 1993, extending their custody.

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. In keeping with the Law on Criminal Procedure, I proposed to the trial chamber to extend their custody following the initial period of 30 days given the fact that there were still reasons in existence which dictated that they should be held in custody as prescribed by the Law on Criminal Procedure. Following my proposal, they issued the decision we saw a moment ago on the screen.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have the two documents admitted, be it separately or as a single exhibit, and marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll mark them for identification. Separately.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D3079 and MFI D3080 respectively, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we next have 1D07832 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what this is, and does it originate from your court, and are you familiar with the people sitting on -- on this chamber?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm familiar with this case, and Obrad Tasovac was the person accused, and he was pronounced guilty for the crime of murder from Article 36, paragraph 1. The victim was Anto Kamenjasevic. I was in charge of investigation in this case. It concerned murder, as we can see, which took place in September 1992. The person who was killed was Anto Kamenjasevic, a Croat. Following the murder, the same day, Obrad Tasovac was detained and I pronounced his custody. After the appropriate procedure was conducted by the Military Court, this judgement was handed down, although I can't see what the sentence was?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we scroll up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do know that the first instance court of the Military Court in Bijeljina sentenced him to four years and six months' imprisonment. After the military prosecution appealed, the prosecution with the command of the East Bosnia Corps, the Supreme Military Court acknowledge the Prosecution appeal and changed the sentence. It reversed their decision and sentenced the accused to nine years of imprisonment, which is twice as much than was decided by the first instance Military Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us what was the ethnicity of the perpetrator?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Obrad Tasovac is a Serb. The Tasovac family hail from Priboj, near Ugljevik or Lopare.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we mark this for identification?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We'll do that.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D3081, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have 07833 next.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with this case and the chamber that you probably presided over?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am familiar with both.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Tell us, briefly, who the perpetrator is, what did he do, and who the victim was, as well as to what the judgement was.

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Boro Zigic was accused for the crime of theft of the vehicle. In May 1992, he stole a passenger vehicle from a Muslim. I don't know what his name is, but it should be in the judgement.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we scroll up?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I think it's Mirsad Topalovic.

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. A criminal report was submitted, an investigation was conducted, and the Military Court, that is to say, the trial chamber I presided over, pronounced the accused guilty and issued a probationary sentence of three months with a suspended sentence of one year. Actually, suspended sentence of four months with a probationary period of one year.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And the vehicle was returned to the victim?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. When the sentence was being decided upon, the trial chamber took into account some mitigating circumstances. It seems that the perpetrator had been wounded and repented following the crime, and that is why he was only sentenced to -- received a suspended sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The perpetrator was a Serb, and the victim Muslim?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have this marked for identification?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D3082, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we next have 1D07834.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please tell us something about the document. You also presided in this case.

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It is another case of the Military Court in Bijeljina where I acted as the presiding judge, and I issued this judgement for two accused, Dragan Stojanovic and Brano Ilic. They stole certain immovable and movable property from unknown owners in the village of Srednja Trnova which was populated by Muslims and was abandoned at the time. On a certain day although I can't see it exactly when --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go down the page to see it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So in mid-November 1992, they stole certain property from unknown owners such as agricultural machinery. It amounted to theft, and they were also -- also received a suspended sentence.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go to the next page? [In English] Next page, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. They were sentenced to two years with a probationary period of one year. It was a rather stringent sentence. It was our practice to apply a particular policy when it comes to the crimes such as this one, which is not as serious as murder or rape, and given the fact that they were members of the VRS, it was our position that even a suspended sentence had sufficient effect. And if the probation was violated in any way, it -- the suspended sentence would be activated on the spot and they would have to go to gaol.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you slow down a bit. The interpreters will be grateful.

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this MFI'd.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D3083, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we next have 1D07835.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does this originate from your court, and did you know the presiding judge, Radisa Bojicic?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the case?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It is a judgement handed down by the aforementioned judge as a presiding judge in the first instance court. The accused was Petrovic -- Bozidar Petrovic, who was convicted for theft. He also received a suspended sentence. If we go to the next page, I'll be able to tell you how long.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go down the page?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So he received a suspended sentence in the duration of three months for the probationary period of one year. For the same reasons I mentioned a moment ago, the first instance court was of the opinion that, by virtue of this decision, the point of sentencing was reached.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can I read out the first line. It is stated he is guilty, that on the 26th of February, 1993, around 10.00, in Brcko, in the settlement of Klanac, he stole some shelves from an abandoned house and courtyard. So in this case, too, the owners were unknown.

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but the settlement was -- or used to be inhabited by Muslims. So the victims were Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have this MFI'd.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: MFI D3084, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we next have 1D07836.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with this case, and do you know the presiding judge and the chamber?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is a judgement of the first instance court in Bijeljina. The presiding judge was Bojanic Radisa, and he pronounced Branko Lukic guilty for the crime of theft. He visited an abandoned house in Gorica, which was a Croatian village, whereby he stole some property that is enumerated in the explanation or reasons of the judgement. He's pronounced guilty and received a suspended sentence. If we go down the page, I'll be able to tell you how long.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go down the page, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the suspended sentence of four months with a probation of one year.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So he stole a stove, two tables, lawn-mowers, and a trailer for a passenger vehicle?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have this MFI'd?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: MFI D3085, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. 1D07837, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you know this trial chamber? Are you familiar with this case?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Also it is the Military Court in Bijeljina. Kitic Ljubomir is the presiding judge, and the accused person is Dusan Arsenic from Vucilovac, near Brcko. He stole some goods from an abandoned house or abandoned houses, a sewing machine, a table, that is to say, movable property, from abandoned Muslim houses, thereby committing the crime of theft. Again he received a suspended sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It seems that it's not a suspended sentence.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we scroll down a bit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Possibly. Yes. Yes. He was sentenced to prison in -- to one year and three months in prison, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Because he looted abandoned houses; right?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We'll mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D3086, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. 1D07838, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with this case?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Again this is a judgement of the Military Court in Bijeljina. Ljubomir Kitic is the presiding judge, and the accused person, Milan Peric, was found guilty, because in the month of May, 1992, he stole from the company of Usor in Brcko, which was in a combat zone. He stole a PC and also a monitor, and we do not -- and we do not see the rest.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please speak slower, because I think you also said that it was a state-owned firm. It's not reflected in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So he stole this and he was found guilty.

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be marked for identification?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In any case of theft, the goods are returned to the owner if the owner is known. Also, if you look at the bottom of the page, you will see that he received a suspended sentence, and I'll tell you exactly what that was. If we can see the bottom of the page. Five months' suspended sentence with a probation period of two years.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D3087, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D07839. So there's just one more left.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with this case?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Again, it is a judgement of the Military Court in Bijeljina. Spasojevic Jezdimir was the presiding judge. Radovanovic Cviko, Radovanovic Milorad are the accused persons. They are from the village of Gornja Krcina, municipality of Ugljevik. They committed the crime of theft. And could we now again see the bottom of the page, please. In the village of Trsunovo Brdo, that was a Muslim-populated village, there were several abandoned houses there, and they stole boards from those houses, a couch, two armchairs, a stove, also some wire and so on. So the crime was theft. Again I think that they received a suspended sentence. Could we look at the next page so that we see what the time period involved was?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next page, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What is the ethnic background of the perpetrators?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Serbs. They're Serbs. And it is the inhabitants of Trsunovo Brdo, a Muslim-populated village, that were the victims.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: However, the property had been abandoned at the point when these goods were stolen?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be MFI'd?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: MFI D3088, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bojanovic, did you have contacts and consultations within the military judiciary? Did you have insight into the doctrine, positions, views taken by the other military courts?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Since there was a war going on, the military courts that were established attached to corps, and they were quite far away, so there were first instance courts. The Supreme Military Court had the following practice: That the chamber of the second instance court, the Supreme Military Court, would visit the lower-ranking courts including the one in Bijeljina. When the criminal chamber was in session and then together with the criminal chamber of the Supreme Military Court, we would accommodate our views and have a joint position with regard to sentencing policy and all other matters that were important for the work of the military judiciary.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know whether in any court at any instance any crime had been hushed up, especially on ethnic grounds, or that there was any kind of discrimination on ethnic grounds?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: As far as the Military Court in Bijeljina is concerned, where I worked, there was no hushing up in any single case or there weren't even any attempts to that effect. No pressure was brought to bear from any quarters to protect a perpetrators -- a perpetrator regardless of background, ethnic or religious background. No one ever asked me to do any such thing. We never did any such thing. I cannot speak about other military courts now, but I am really not aware of any such thing. I have not heard of any such thing, that there was any hushing up or discrimination in any Military Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bojanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At this point in time, I have no further questions of this witness, Your Excellency.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bojanovic, your evidence in chief has been admitted in most part in writing, and you'll be now cross-examined by the representative of the Office of the Prosecutor, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Bojanovic. Do you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, good day.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You stated in paragraph 11 of your statement, and you've testified about it a little bit this morning, that you conducted an investigation against Cvetkovic and Jurosevic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You said you took statements from two rape victims and that one of the victims expressed disbelief that a trial would be conducted.

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You, in fact, reinforced to her that a trial would indeed take place.

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: But you released both suspects six days before you completed your investigation, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And in fact that was the document that we looked at earlier dated the 22nd of January, 1993, which is now D3078. But you were also conducting an investigation in relation to these two accused for the murder under Article 36 of -- of a Muslim man who you named this morning.

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but I explained that to you as I was answering the questions that were put to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: But instead of releasing him, you could have gone to the Military Supreme Court --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please make a pause between questions and answers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: -- to extend the custody for another three months [overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, no. Ms. Sutherland, you need to repeat your question because you overlapped.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: My apologies, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Bojanovic, you could have gone to the Supreme Court to extend the custody for another three months as you were legally entitled to do under Article 197 of the criminal procedure law, couldn't you?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but since the reasons prescribed by the Law on Criminal Procedure were no longer there, they were released from custody, but that doesn't mean that they were pardoned in any way. Criminal proceedings continued against them. I found that at that point in time there was no reason for them to remain in custody, and all of that is in line with the Law on Criminal Procedure. All the reasons that were mentioned when remanding them in custody were no longer there, and therefore the court decided on releasing them from custody. I repeat that they were not freed of any kind of criminal responsibility. It is simply that they were released from custody.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we could have 65 ter number 24664, please. And if we can look at Article 191 of the law.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Bojanovic, what we have in front of us is Articles 190 to Article 201 of the Law of Criminal Procedure. Article 191 of the law sets out when pre-trial custody shall and may be ordered. It talks about a person being a danger of -- of flight, interfering with witnesses, and it's mandatory to detain until trial persons that are charged with a criminal act for which the law prescribes a death penalty. Now, Article -- under Article 36 of the Criminal Code, and that's Exhibit P06144, you know, don't you, that a person sentenced -- that the penalty for a person who kills another while behaving in a wantonly violent manner is able to be sentenced to a term of imprisonment of at least ten years or the death penalty. You know that, don't you?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think that we are understanding each other. What is the case that you are referring to? I'm still talking about the Jurosevic-Cvetkovic case, and it is the crime of rape that is involved. I don't think that we're understanding each other.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: These two accused were also charged with murder, were they not?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that. Believe me. That was 20 years ago. I remember full well that I carried out an investigation with regard to the crime of rape.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could we have D01481, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Bojanovic, we can see here that this is a request from the military prosecutor to the Military Court to expand the investigation.

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sorry. This is for the -- from -- from prosecutor Drinic to request the investigation for murder, I'm sorry. Now you know subsequently, the next day, the following day -- in fact, on that day, on the 29th of October, you interviewed Cvetkovic?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And then the following day, on the 30th of -- and -- sorry, the record of interview is D01482. The following day, on the 30th of October, the military prosecutor then wrote to the Military Court and requested to expand the investigation to include the rapes, and that's Exhibit D01483. So instead of releasing these accused, you could have gone under Article 197 of the Law of Criminal Procedure before the Military Supreme Court and extended their custody for another three months.

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, my assessment was probably that there was -- that it wasn't proper to do that. It did not mean automatically that a person would have to remain in custody until the trial started even when the crime of murder is involved. It was customary to release accused persons from custody even in such situations, and that is probably what I assessed then. There was custody for 30 days, and then after that, in the decision extending custody for another 60 days, the reasons are stated.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In line 23, the witness said it was not uncustomary. So it basically means the same thing that is reflected in the transcript, that it was customary?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We can continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Bojanovic, what more did you need to complete the investigation? You had the circumstances of the murder. You had the statements of the rape victims. You had the records of interview of the accused. You had an eyewitness to the rapes. You had information from the military that they were members of the military. The only requirement that you needed was the observations of the doctor. Why would you release someone who's being -- on suspicion of murder and two rapes?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I repeat to you what I said to you a moment ago and that is that probably I assessed the reasons why he was kept in custody, and when those reasons were no longer there and when the 90th day of custody expired, then I reached a decision releasing him from custody, because the reasons for which he was sent to custody was no longer there. That did not mean at all that they were freed of criminal responsibility. As far as I know, they were prosecuted and tried before the court in Brcko and ultimately convicted.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Bojanovic, you stated at transcript page 49 to 50 this morning that they were convicted by the Bijeljina District Court. In fact, they were convicted in absentia. No. I'm sorry, I take that back. I take that back. They in fact -- they, in fact, according to -- to other court records, Jurosevic was acquitted in 2006 and Cvetkovic was transferred to a war crimes court in 2009. The case that you referred to a moment ago about the Bijeljina District Court was Mihajlovic, not Cvetkovic and Jurosevic. Okay. In paragraph 14 of your statement, where you talk about the Mihajlovic case, basically the only thing you did in this case was to issue a wanted notice because he was a fugitive; correct?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: AND that wanted notice is D01478.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: In fact, he shouldn't have been released and as you stated at transcript page 50 earlier this morning, that he had been unlawfully released. Now, the investigation wasn't completed at the time that he was released. In fact, Exhibit D0147 -- sorry, 65 ter 24711 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Sutherland, why don't you wait for some time to hear the witness's answer. Given that it is being translated, you have to wait a bit. I'm not sure the witness had the opportunity to answer the previous question about the acquittal of Jurosevic. Did you want to say something in response to that, Mr. Bojanovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as Jurosevic is concerned, no, because I expressed what it was that I knew and obviously my knowledge had been incomplete. I really did not know that that's the way the case ended, believe me. It was a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And this one.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I would like to say that Madam Prosecutor is not right when she says - I mean, speaking of Mihajlovic Rado - that he was unlawfully released, because a decision had been taken on the basis of the Law on Criminal Procedure to release him from custody and this was done with the knowledge of the prosecutor's office. As I already said this morning, I was in charge of the indictment as the president of the chamber and once I found out that this person was a fugitive, I ordered the MUP to issue a wanted notice. But I'm still saying that the prosecutor is not right when she says that the decision on the release from custody is unlawful. It is based on the law. And in my decision there is certainly a reference to the reasons that I took into account, and as far as I know, the prosecutor did not complain at that point in time either.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Probably there was a mistake in translation. At transcript page 50, lines 3 to 4, in answering the question about Rade Mihajlovic, you said this: "However, the person was a fugitive. And I had been in custody." That's the point I clarified that, not you, the accused. Mihajlovic had been in custody. And the transcript goes on like this: "And had unlawfully released." So it sounded like you confirmed that Mihajlovic's release was unlawful. That's the point of the question. So could you clarify what you said there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that when the indictment was issued against Rado Mihajlovic, he had already been released from custody. I do not agree with what the Prosecutor is saying, that he was unlawfully released. I repeat that once again that it is clearly stated in the decision on releasing him from custody what the reasons were for making that kind of decision. Even the military prosecutor's office that started the investigation against him did not appeal that decision. So it is wrong to state that he was unlawfully released from custody. I repeat for the umpteenth time today that releasing a person from custody does not mean that the person who is being released from custody is being freed of criminal responsibility. Quite simply, he's being released from custody and he can defend himself not being in detention, and that is a system that exists in all legal systems and that is something that we applied at that point in time as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Mihajlovic [sic], if we look at 65 ter number 24709, which is the order releasing the accused dated the 30th of December, 1992, we can see simply that it says because his detention -- one-month detention has been extended for two months and that period is up, then he shall be released right away. Do you see that there?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And I don't see anything unlawful here. On the basis of what did you conclude that this was --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Bojanovic --

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: -- an unlawful decision?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Bojanovic, as the Presiding Judge has already advised you, that was what is -- was in the transcript that you said this morning on transcript page 50, and then you were given an opportunity to clarify that. So my question was based on what you -- what is in the transcript of what you had said earlier today. We're agreed on that? My point --

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Then I must have been misinterpreted. That is not what I said, that is not what I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: My point being Mr. Mihajlovic should never have been released because, again, under Article 197, the investigative judge could have and should have gone to the Supreme Court and sought an additional three months because at that time the investigation hadn't been completed. It was a murder under Article 36, so it was a serious crime, and in fact we -- we know that where -- where a murder is -- is done in a wanton way and that is, this accused Mihajlovic fired 25 rounds from an automatic rifle from a distance of about 50 centimetres at the head, the neck and the chest of the injured party, Enes Tabakovic, while he was in bed in a military barracks while he was detained. So isn't that something that should have happened and didn't, but instead, the Serb accused gets released?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, you said yourself that the judge could have, but it wasn't that he had to do it. The law allows the possibility for extending custody by an order of the Supreme Court, but probably he determined that there was no reason to extend detention. And I don't see why you insist on that. As far as I know and you know that Rade Mihajlovic was convicted for that crime --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Again, Mr. Bojanovic --

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: -- so there was no influence on --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You said that he was convicted by the Bijeljina District Court. He was convicted in absentia in 2001, was he not?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But the judge who made the decision to release him from custody pending trial didn't know that he would flee.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And -- and you said that you took on the case after -- after the indictment had been issued and you said that you issued the indictment. In fact, Mr. Blagojevic from the district prosecutor -- from the military prosecutor's office issued the indictment against Rade Mihajlovic, didn't he? Not yourself. And that was on the 5th of January, 1993. That's Exhibit D01476.

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I never said that I issued the indictment. I think it's your mistake, madam. The prosecutor's office issued it, and it was issued to me as the president of the chamber, as the presiding judge. We know very well who issues the indictments and who is obliged to act in accordance with them.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I note -- I note the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We'll have a break for 45 minutes and resume at 18 past 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please continue, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Bojanovic, just before the break we were talking about the accused Mihajlovic, and we had looked at the decision to release him on the 30th of December, 1992, which was seven days before the decision to discontinue the investigation.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we could have 65 ter number 24711.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you see that there?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: So the accused was released a week later -- sorry, so he was released prior to the investigation being completed. Then a week later, the decision comes out to discontinue the investigation. And then you say that you came into the picture and you issued a wanted notice because he was a fugitive. It's right, isn't it, that you'd summoned him a couple of times to appear but, of course, surprise, surprise, charged with murder and he's been released, he's not going to turn up, is he?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you want me to declare -- to say anything about this decision to discontinue investigation, or -- it seems to me you put two questions. In this decision to discontinue investigation that I see on the monitor ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, please continue, Mr. Bojanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the statement of reasons, it reads that the military prosecutor, on the 4th of January, 1993, decided to discontinue investigation, and the judge acted completely in accordance with the Law on Criminal Procedure given the fact that the person in charge of conducting criminal procedure dropped it. I do know, however, that following this, the prosecution decided to reinstate the investigation against the accused Mihajlovic. I think we also scheduled a search, but we had information that he was unavailable. He was a fugitive. And then we ordered an order to the -- we ordered the MUP to issue a wanted notice.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And then, as we know, he was then tried in absentia some months later by the Bijeljina court. Mr. Bojanovic, just quickly I want to take you back --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. I think we're having a habit of a lot of comments by the Prosecution without putting questions to the witness. If she wants to make a comment, she should ask the witness to comment on it not -- she's not giving evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Point taken.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Bojanovic, would you like to see the Bijeljina indictment again?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, please, show it to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: D01479, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you see the first paragraph, "in the absence of the accused whom has been tried while absent"?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I can just take you quickly back to the accused Cvetkovic and Jurosevic. You said today earlier at transcript page 61 that you didn't know that they were charged with murder. I just want to take you quickly to your decision that released them.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And that's D3078, please. Exhibit D3078.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. With respect to 65 ter number 24711, the decision ending the investigation, is that being tendered?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How about the previous one? 24709 --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And 24709, yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we don't have any objections to either of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And also I'd like to admit the Law on Criminal Proceedings, 24664.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We'll admit them all shall we give the number it turn one by one.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. 65 ter number 24664 will be Exhibit P6178. 65 ter number 24709 will be Exhibit P6179. And 65 ter number 24711 will be Exhibit P6180.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Bojanovic, this is the decision of the 22nd of January, 1993, releasing Cvetkovic and Jurosevic. And in the statement of reasons it says they had committed the crime of murder.

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And if we could quickly go to exhibit -- sorry, 65 ter 1D07241.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Bojanovic, this is a document dated the 28th of January, 1993. Now, we do have an English translation of this document. It says that the court has completed -- and this is signed by you. Were you -- it's typed signed your name. This court has completed an investigation on Cvetkovic and Jurosevic suspected of committing a crime under Article 36. And Article 36 is murder, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: This is a standard letter accompanying the case file after an investigation has been closed, and it goes back to the prosecution for further action. It contains my order which says that the investigation was discontinued and that the case file should be forwarded to the prosecutor's office for further action in keeping with Article 174 of the Law on Criminal Procedure. The date, the 26th of January, 1993. Perhaps the 28th.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Bojanovic?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And it went to --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Bojanovic, I'm not going to go back over the event relating to that case. We dealt with that earlier today. I was simply showing you these documents to remind you that these gentlemen were charged with murder which is contained in documents that are signed by you. So I want to move now to paragraph 16 of your statement, and there you say that in the second half of 1992, the position was taken that Military Courts should try perpetrators who committed criminal offences while on duty, and that regular courts should have jurisdiction for all other criminal offences. Was this the Bijeljina Military Court or -- and/or all military courts in the Republika Srpska? Who are you referring to there?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I discussed matters in general for the entire military judiciary. There was this dilemma at the beginning when the military courts began working as to their real competence.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Bojanovic, it's right, though, that that didn't happen in 1992 or, in fact, at least right the way through 1993.

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm afraid I didn't understand.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Let's look at exhibit -- sorry, 65 ter 24713.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: We can see that this is some documents relating to an accused, Miladin Djuric, who is charged under Article 36, and this is a case that you dealt with, where you sentenced Miladin Djuric of Serb ethnicity to two years and eight months for the manslaughter of another Serb.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we can go to the verdict which is on English page 5 of the document, dated the 1st of February, 1993, we can see there -- if we can have page 5 of the English translation. I don't know why it's not appearing.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The circumstances of this case -- do you recall this case, Mr. Bojanovic, Miladin Djuric?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And the circumstances --

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Reading the document, it does ring a bell.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Well, we can see on the first page of the B/C/S the circumstances. And it says on -- on the 15th of November, 1992, he fired --

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: -- in a place in Batkovic, when he was under the influence of alcohol, he fired from a sniper rifle and hit someone who was sitting on the chair. So this is something that's -- that's off duty, and it's being dealt with you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we can go if we can scroll through the B/C/S, then, if we can't get the English on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And we can see that you were in the trial chamber.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we can go to the next page, please. And the next page. Until we get to the document the 1st of February, 1993. And the following. There.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you see there you're in the trial chamber? So this is an offence that's occurring in -- in November 1992. The trial's on the 1st of February, 1993. Do you agree that this is something that's off duty and it's being dealt with by the Military Court?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, you see that's what I said in my statement. At first we were going back and forth on the issue of subject matter jurisdiction, and only later on did we take the position that the military courts were competent to try for crimes committed by military personnel on duty. At first we tried all of them --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Bojanovic, if I can interrupt. Your statement says in paragraph 16: "In the second half of 1992, the position was taken that military courts should try perpetrators who committed criminal offences while on duty and that regular courts should have jurisdiction for all other criminal offences." Now I've just given you one example where we have an off-duty military person who is tried before the court, in fact tried by you, for an offence that happens off duty. If I can take you to another example.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: -- I'd like to intervene. In paragraph 16 there seems to be a mistake. It's about 1993, given the fact that the military courts began work in August and September 1992. So this is a mistake. And I seem to have missed it when reading it. As well as the Defence team, they didn't pick up on it either. The Military Court in Bijeljina only initiated initial investigations in August 1992, in the second half of 1992, when there was no position yet on the issue regarding cases as this one.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Okay. If we could have 65 ter number 24714.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Bojanovic, this is another case that you dealt with, Vojko Prodanovic. And again, his offence occurred on the 17th of November, 1992. He was -- he threw a hand grenade on the terrace of a house and, as a result, another Serb was killed, and he was sentenced by you in the chamber, trial chamber, which included yourself, to 13 years' imprisonment for murder of another Serb, and that trial took place in June 1993. So again we have an off-duty incident being tried by the Military Court. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I've told you already that in this paragraph 16, 1993 is a mistake. Actually, instead of 1992, it should be 1993. By 1993, we tried all such cases that were referred to by the military prosecutor. In the situation when we had an immediate threat of war in Republika Srpska, all able-bodied men were considered to be soldiers. In keeping with that, all crimes they committed were tried by military courts. Only in 1993 did we take the position that only such crimes committed by persons on duty in their units should be tried and heard by the --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. -- Mr. --

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: -- the Military Court.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: -- Bojanovic, you mentioned that you weren't restricting this to the Bijeljina Military Court, so I'll show you another document.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And that's P06146. And this is a Banja Luka Military Court document. It's a judgement dated the 21st of October, 1993, where again we have a military person who commits a crime off duty and he is tried by the Military Court.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: That's another example, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: It seems that the crime was committed on the 7th of August, 1992. A murder was carried out that day, that is to say, the beginning of the period when the military courts became operational.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And he's being tried --

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: All cases initiated --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And he's being tried in October 1993, isn't he?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: It was the position that all cases which were initiated by regular courts to be concluded there. Once we took the position that as of that moment on criminal procedure should be undertaken by regular courts --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Okay --

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: -- well, that later on was transferred to the military courts.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Bojanovic, I have two brief matters I want to deal with. One is in paragraph 18 of -- sorry, three brief matters. One is in paragraph 18 of your statement. You say that in February 1993, you were called to a double homicide in the Vanekov Mlin prison and that allegedly a soldier of a unit of the 2nd Krajina Brigade had killed two Muslim detainees. And as a result of your investigation and the fact that you knew that one of the victims was from Kljuc and one of the soldiers was also from Kljuc, you issued an arrest warrant -- sorry, given that you only issued an arrest warrant for an unidentified perpetrator. That's what you said in paragraph 18, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: First of all, I didn't know any of the victims. That is your mistake in interpretation. There is another small intervention in this respect. The murder took place in the yard of a building belonging to the Zitopromet company, and the persons who were victims were accommodated in Batkovic in the -- on the military farm.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's intervention, could the witness kindly slow down.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Bojanovic, you've been asked to slow down by the interpreters. And we'll get to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you -- could you repeat your answer starting from the part where you mentioned Batkovic on the military farm.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Vanekov Mlin, it belonged to the Zitopromet company from Bijeljina. The persons who were victims were accommodated in the collection centre at Ekonomija, the military farm in Batkovic. And on that day, they were on work duty in Zitopromet, in Vanekov Mlin.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Bojanovic, it wouldn't have taken much further investigation to work out who the perpetrator was, would it? You knew that a unit had stopped at the barracks. You knew that that unit was from Kljuc. You knew that the perpetrator had a family member who had been killed in a place near Kljuc. With just a little bit of further investigation, you could have found out the perpetrator, could you not?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Listen, it's not the court that looks for the perpetrator of a crime but it's, rather, the police. In accordance with the Law on Criminal Proceedings, on the following day we drew up an order to issue a wanted notice for an unidentified person. I suppose you have this document. And we or, rather, I as the judge on duty made a report with it with a photo file and I gave it to the prosecutor's office which was in charge. A further investigation of the perpetrators is in the jurisdiction of the police and I issued them the order to issue a wanted notice. I didn't know who these persons were and -- except, as I said in my report, that these were the members of the 2nd Krajina Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You're an investigating judge, aren't you? The investigating judge conducts the investigation?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Bojanovic, you mentioned in these additional paragraphs that were added on Sunday to your statement robbery and rape, which was one case, and a murder of a Croat victim was another. All the other cases that you mention in your statement were all to do with theft. Now you would agree with me, would you not, that there was not one Article 142 crime - and that's war crimes against the civilian population - that was ever heard before the Bijeljina Military Court during the war, was there?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, but as you are well aware, the criminal proceedings --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And -- and --

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Please don't interrupt me. The criminal proceedings are not initiated by the court but, rather, by the prosecutor's office which is in charge. And probably if the prosecutor's office had addressed us with such a request, the court would have acted accordingly.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The fact is very few Serbs were tried and convicted for crimes against non-Serb persons; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, you are not right. Believe me, we didn't count how many members of which ethnicity were indicted. We simply tried all cases where there was an indictment and where evidence was available. Believe me, none of us ever made any differences about the damaged party in any case being a Serb, Croat, or Muslim, which we proved in the sentences which we have enclosed and I suppose that you have some of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Bojanovic, I want to deal very, very quickly now with the Batkovic detention facility which you mentioned a moment ago. Was this a remand prison?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What was it, then?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: It was a collection centre, as far as I know. We as the Military Court were not in charge of this facility. We had a military detention [Realtime transcript read in error "defence"] or military remand prison which was part of the Military Court, and there -- the persons who were held there were those whose custody was ordered by the Military Court. And the army was in jurisdiction of Batkovic and we had no contact whatsoever with this facility.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Interestingly, the president of the Supreme Court -- Military Supreme Court said a few days ago that it was a remand prison, and that's at transcript 34094. You say that it was --

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. I think we -- it's not proper for Ms. Sutherland to give evidence or to make a statement without putting a question to the witness. Dr. Karadzic was constantly being upbraided for that during his case. So if she has --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: -- something to ask the witness, she should. Otherwise she shouldn't be making those comments.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Bojanovic, you say that it wasn't a remand prison and that it was a facility where persons were held whose custody was ordered by the Military Court. Where -- where would we find all of the -- all of the orders in relation to keeping these detainees for months and months on end? Where we would find those?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Believe me, I don't know. But I repeat, the Military Court didn't have any jurisdiction over this facility so I think you would have to look for it in the army, which secured and protected this facility.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I understood your last answer to be that -- that Batkovic was under the jurisdiction of the army and therefore the Military Court.

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No. You are changing my words and my statement. I didn't say that a single time today. The Military Court had its own detention facility which was in part of the building where the Military Court was, and all the persons who were in custody by the order of the Military Court were held there. The Military Court did not have any jurisdiction over the facility in Batkovic. So if it's a provocation, it's inappropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Page -- just a second. Page 83, line 22, the transcript is -- noted as like this: "We had a military defence" -- or I will begin from -- start from the beginning. It was a question about Batkovic. This is your answer: "It was a collection centre, as far as I know. We as the Military Court were not in charge of this facility. We had a military defence or military remand prison which was part of the Military Court." What did you say, "We had a military defence"? Is this what you said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I didn't say "defence." No, there's a mistake probably because I talk so fast. We had a detention facility which was part of the building where the Military Court worked and this was the only facility in which we held detainees who were detained on our orders.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, I understood to that effect, but in the future please speak very slowly. Yes, Ms. Sutherland, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Bojanovic, the Eastern Bosnia Corps command -- the Batkovic military camp came under the Eastern Bosnia Corps, did it not?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I suppose so.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And the Eastern Bosnia and -- and the Bijeljina Military Court dealt with crimes committed in the area of responsibility of the Eastern Bosnia Corps, did they not?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Did you ever visit the Batkovic camp?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Not as a judge of the Military Court. A couple of times I went to this facility as I had Muslim friends from Bijeljina. Specifically, a close family friend of mine, my kum, is from Bijeljina. Some acquaintances who were mostly living abroad asked if cigarettes, food or a letter could be taken to him. And a couple of times I went to this facility as a private person and I brought to these people accommodated there cigarettes or food or letters, but I never visited it officially as a captain of the army of Republika Srpska or a judge on duty. I never visited the facility in such capacity, but I certainly went to the facility five or six times.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And these people that you went to visit were Muslim civilians who had been detained there?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And in fact there were a large number of civilians who were brought there by the Serb authorities, wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: There weren't so many of them there when I went there. The last time I went was in 1995, perhaps in August or September, I wouldn't say that there were more than perhaps a few hundred people. I didn't see them because the guards would take out the people to whom I was supposed to deliver the cigarettes or food or letters.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Did you -- did you go to the Batkovic camp in 1992?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I think not during that year. I believe that it could have been in 1993 that I went there for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you know the commander of the -- he was the commander of the East Bosnia Corps, Novica Simic?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I knew him. He was the second commander. The first one before him was -- I believe his name was Colonel Mile Ilic, unless I'm mistaken, when the Military Court was established. It was only then, but very soon afterwards, I think after the setting up of the Military Court, that Novica Simic, General, was the corps commander. Yes, I did know him.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: He testified at a trial here about the Batkovic prison camp. When he -- where he said that he took over duties and formed a commission to establish a real state of affairs in the Batkovic camp because he had heard some contradictory reports on his arrival. He goes on to say that the report that he received from this commission that he set up was alarming and unbelievable for him because there were persons in the camp who could not under any circumstances be considered prisoners of war. He said there were about 80 persons, civilians, amongst them a few were underage. They were simply picked up from their homes in Zvornik and Kozluk and brought there. He also said when he testified that he ordered that these persons were to be released. And when he asked them where they wanted to go, some said they wanted to go back to their homes because some of the local authorities had collected them from their homes, rounded them up, and put them in a military camp. And he said that this was inappropriate because it was a -- it was a prisoner of war camp and there were no grounds for these people to be here. He said: "I knew that the civilian authorities would attack me for this reason, and that's why I rang up General Gvero and told him what I'd decided." Is this what I've just described to you by -- that General Novica Simic said, is this something that you had heard about the Batkovic camp when you went there, when you said that you went there on six other occasions?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What I knew, and that was the opinion at the time, was that these were prisoners of war. Whether there were any civilians there as well and how they had been brought there, this is something I really don't know. I know that the last time when I visited the place, I think I was bringing cigarettes to some young men. I believe that they were from somewhere in the vicinity of Srebrenica or Bratunac. I think they told me that they were taken prisoner somewhere around Zvornik. This is what I know and that's all. Believe me.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
